answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce, slashable stake before it can post jobs or earn reputation. A verifier randomly assigns overlapping tasks to agents; identities that collude to endorse the same false result risk losing their deposits when independent evidence exposes it. This makes a nebula of disposable accounts costly: each needs capital, and coordinating them risks forfeiture. A willow of long-lived, honest agents gains value through accumulated history, while a canyon between attack cost and expected reward deters profitable Sybils.
